sentences.text:
Shri Sanjay K. Agarwal, Senior Advocate with Shri Rahul
 counsel for the applicant.
Shri Akhilendra Singh, G.A. for respondent/State.
Trial court record has been received.
Heard on admission.
Trial court record perused.
Prima facie, this revision seems to be arguable.
Hence, admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A.No.15149/2024, an application under Section 397/401 of Cr.P.C for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail pending the revision.

The applicant has been convicted for commission of offence under Section 7 read with section 16(1)(ka)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 01 year and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation vide judgment dated 03.02.2024 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Katni, District Katni (MP) in Criminal Case No.145/2020 (State of M.P. Vs. Subhash Pillai).

sentences.text: An appeal was preferred by the applicant challenging the judgment of conviction and order of sentence, but learned Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Katni District Katni (MP) vide 2 CRR-2984-2024 judgment dated 14.06.2024 passed in Criminal Appeal No.31/2024 has partly allowed the appeal upholding the conviction of the applicant, but modified the sentence by reducing it from one year RI to six months RI and fine amount from Rs.1,000/-.

1 defend himself.

entities.text: Subhash Pillai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel has challenged the legality, propriety and correctness of the judgments passed by the courts below.
It is submitted that applicant is in jail for more than a month.
Applicant has fair chances to succeed in appeal.
The sentence awarded by the first appellate court is six months R.I.
Therefore, if the execution of jail sentence of applicant is not suspended, the purpose of filing this revision petition would become futile.
The applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the terms and conditions imposed by the Court.
Thus, it is prayed that custodial jail sentence of the applicant may be suspended and he be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer for grant of bail.

Considering the short nature of sentence including the detention period of the applicant and the fact that there is no possibility of final hearing of this revision in near future, I am inclined to suspend the 3 CRR-2984-2024 remaining jail sentence of the applicant, pending the revision petition.
Consequently, I.A.No.15149 of 2024 is allowed.
It is directed that the execution of jail sentence of applicant - Subhash Pillai is hereby suspended subject to depositing the entire fine amount, if not already deposited.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond to a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court on 26.11.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Subhash Pillai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55128515/
